title: BlueRidge Q1 inference health & growth checkpoint
summary: Quarterly health check focusing on usage trends, unexpected cost spike in February, reliability incidents tied to a misconfigured autoscale policy, and roadmap alignment for expanding real-time recommendations. Agreed to run a focused pilot on optimized batching and KV prefix caching for high-frequency endpoints and to share cost breakdown and security docs.
topics: autoscale and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed Feb cost breakdown and per-route token report by 2027-03-18
Customer to provide sample traffic curve for recommendations endpoint by 2027-03-19
Ethan to run a micro-benchmark on 8-bit quantized model variant and share results by 2027-03-22
action_items: Ethan Chu - run quantization micro-benchmark and share CSV results - 2027-03-22
Samira Patel - deliver per-route cost breakdown and pricing sheet - 2027-03-18
Maya Thompson - upload 48-hour traffic capture for rec endpoint to shared drive - 2027-03-19
Lena Morales - open pilot playbook and invite stakeholders - 2027-03-17
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-15 15:00 UTC | Duration 58m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (CSM), Maya (BlueRidge Head of ML), Eric (Platform Eng), Jamal (CTO), Priya (Product).

00:00 Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time for the q1 health and growth checkpoint. we'll run about 45, 50 minutes, leave 10 for next steps. can everyone hear me okay?
00:08 Maya (BlueRidge): yeah loud and clear, thanks.
00:12 Jamal (BlueRidge CTO): yep good here.
00:15 Samira: great. quick agenda, usage trends, a cost anomaly we saw in feb, reliability incidents and mitigations, then roadmap alignment for the recommendation product and a proposed pilot. Ethan will lead the technical bits. lena will cover support items.
00:30 Lena (CSM): hi all. brief note, we pulled together the incident timeline and support tickets, will attach the doc after the call.
00:36 Samira: ok first, usage — Ethan?
00:40 Ethan (SE): sure. so overall q1 usage is up 34% q/q driven by rec endpoint and chat support. the rec endpoint now accounts for ~56% of token volume. we noticed a big spike in early feb — an approx 2.8x bump for 48 hours. that aligns with a backend rollout from blue on feb 3? maya, can you confirm?
00:58 Maya: yeah we did a feature toggle rollout the night of feb 2 that changed request fan-out. it should have been gated but a mis-set flag triggered broader sampling. we caught it within a day but tokens were high.
01:12 Ethan: right so costs scaled superlinearly because of long context on those verbose requests and retries from the client side. there were also some cold-start affected requests because the autopilot scale-down threshold was aggressive.
01:26 Eric (Platform): we had some retries, we didn't realize the SDK default was set to 5 retries; we changed client-side to 2 after feb 4.
01:33 Samira: that ties into two mitigation areas — client retry policy and scale configuration. on the platform side, redwood suggested a conservative cooldown and a short warm-up buffer for the rec pool.
01:46 Maya: curious about batching — we get small, frequent requests, can batching help without increasing latency?
01:51 Ethan: yes, there's continuous batching in the runtime. for high QPS small payloads we can group within a 10–20ms window and see large token cost reductions. the trade is tail latency, but we can tune per-route SLOs. also prefix caching (kv cache) works well for repeated contexts, if you have repeated partial prompts — storing the kv per-user session reduces compute.
02:12 Priya (Product): do we have any numbers on batch size vs p99 latency?
02:16 Ethan: rough numbers from similar customers: batching 4–8 into a single infer call increased median by ~8ms but p99 increased by 30–70ms depending on model and sequence length. with pruning and priority routing we can keep p99 < 250ms for many rec use cases. i'll share a small spreadsheet.
02:32 Samira: okay next cost breakdown — lena, can you summarize the feb anomaly and the ongoing run rate?
02:39 Lena: feb cost bump was ~3.1x week-over-week for those 48 hours; total feb invoice was 22% higher than our baseline forecast. outside that period monthly run rate is roughly stable but trending up 12% q/q. we've attached a per-route cost CSV; samira will reshare an annotated version with suggestions on quantization and batching savings.
03:03 Maya: what about dedicated pools? we talked about dedicated last quarter — would that have prevented the spike?
03:10 Samira: dedicated would give predictable throughput and avoids noisy neighbors, but it doesn't prevent client-side retries or misconfig flags that increase request volume. dedicated helps with predictable cost under steady traffic and strict latency SLOs; hybrid approach works well — host rec pool on dedicated, keep chat hosted for burst.
03:24 Jamal: what about autoscale settings — the incident logs mentioned a race between scale-down and a burst. could we set a longer cooldown?
03:31 Ethan: yes, increase min replicas, longer cooldown to avoid thrashing, and configure warm-standby to reduce cold-starts for the rec pool. also a policy to fallback to a lower-cost model variant on heavy load.
03:46 Maya: i'd like the fallback variant but without perceptible quality drop — do you have model-choice guidance?
03:51 Ethan: we recommend two-tier variants: production fp16 and a quantized int8 or 4-bit variant for burst mode. for many ranking tasks int8 gives acceptable quality. we'll run a micro-benchmark on your representative prompts.
04:05 Samira: lena, on the reliability incidents, anything else to call out?
04:09 Lena: incident was primarily the traffic surge plus some request timeouts when a few regional nodes hit memory pressure. we've opened an infra ticket and recommended a regional fallback route and circuit breaker rules. support also confirmed audit logs and request traces were intact for postmortem.
04:24 Eric: the memory pressure was in eu-west region due to deployment overlap — we will change our deployment cadence.
04:28 Samira: good. security/compliance note — Jamal and Maya asked last time about retention and KMS. we did share SOC2 and KMS integration docs in the portal, but i'll re-share the security pack and the private deployment checklist.
04:42 Jamal: yes please, especially the customer-managed KMS flow and audit log retention settings.
04:47 Samira: will do.
04:50 Ethan: moving to the recommended pilot — suggested scope: optimize rec endpoint with 1) per-route batching window tuned to your traffic curve, 2) enable prefix KV caching for repeated sessions, 3) deploy quantized model variant as fallback, 4) measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta over 7 days.
05:10 Maya: sounds good. what's the risk to user-facing latency?
05:14 Ethan: minimal if we tune batching small (10–25ms) and keep a warm pool; fallback only triggers on sustained high load — not for single-user requests.
05:24 Priya: what telemetry will we need from our side? we can provide the request payload histogram and qps by 1-minute bins.
05:31 Samira: that's ideal. Maya, can you get us a 48-hour spike and normal baseline?
05:36 Maya: yes i'll upload by friday.
05:38 Samira: great. now quick pricing note — Samira to send pricing delta and savings scenarios; also if you go dedicated there's a commit model versus burst-only.
05:48 Jamal: ballpark, how many tokens saved after batching + quantization?
05:52 Ethan: examples: batching + caching reduced token compute cost by 35–55% in prior pilots; quantization adds another 10–20% depending on model architecture and quality tolerance. combined, many customers see 40–60% unit cost reduction during optimized windows.
06:12 Maya: wow that would be meaningful.
06:15 Lena: one operational note — we'll need an SLA for the dedicated pool if you choose that; we can draft a commitment proposal.
06:21 Jamal: send SLA options.
06:23 Samira: will do.
06:25 Samira: any blockers for running the pilot?
06:28 Eric: we need a short list of model variants you support and an integration checklist for feature flags.
06:33 Ethan: i'll attach the supported quantized variants and a small playbook for toggling fallback.
06:37 Maya: also access to the dev console for sampling logs would be helpful.
06:41 Samira: okay we'll grant a 30-day dev access scoped to the rec route. lena will set that up.
06:48 Lena: noted.
06:50 Samira: timebox — 20 minutes for pilot setup, then 7 days of run, then readout.
06:55 Priya: internal stakeholders? we'll need product and infra alignment — i'll invite them to the kickoff.
06:59 Jamal: i'll approve the pilot budget up to a threshold, send note to finance after the cost estimate.
07:05 Samira: perfect. now quick Q&A from the team?
07:09 Maya: one more — for audit logs retention, can we set retention to 3 years for compliance?
07:14 Samira: yes, for Private deployments or Dedicated with extended retention we can make that contractual. hosted has configurable retention up to 365 days; for longer we'll need dedicated/private or an add-on.
07:27 Jamal: ok that's reasonable.
07:30 Priya: what about region residency for EU data?
07:33 Samira: we support region pinning for hosted in eu-west and a private VPC for strict residency; both are available and we'll surface the options in the security pack.
07:44 Ethan: small technical detail — if you pin region, KV cache locality matters; we'll recommend co-locating sessions with cache nodes to avoid cross-region fetches.
07:55 Eric: good to know.
07:59 Samira: we're about 40 minutes in, quick recap and next steps. lena going to open pilot playbook and invite stakeholders, samira will send cost breakout and security docs, ethan to run quantization benchmark, maya to upload traffic capture, schedule pilot kickoff 3/24. anything else?
08:20 Maya: no that's it. thanks.
08:24 Samira: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up in writing within 48 hours. end meeting.

Notes: Transcription contains some mis-heard technical terms (e.g., kv cache typed as "k-v cash" in one earlier auto-snippet), occasional speaker attribution confusion around 02:16–02:32 where overlapping talk registered as 'Speaker 1'. Shared artifacts referenced: https://drive.redwood.com/BR-costs-feb.csv (per-route costs), https://redwood.com/security-pack.pdf (security pack), https://redwood.com/pilot-playbook (pilot playbook), pricing sheet (attachment to be sent).

Post-call followup (auto): Samira shared annotated cost CSV and pilot playbook link. Ethan uploaded quick quant benchmark notes in the shared folder (pending full runs).
notes: Customer to consider dedicated pool for rec endpoint if cost trending continues
Pilot will prioritize batching + caching before committing to dedicated capacity
Finance approval pending for pilot budget
private_notes: Customer asked for a 30-day dev console scoped access and a sample of the quantized model list; CSM to provision and redact any PII in uploaded traffic before sharing.
